title: Paying for Medical Treatment in Türkiye: Bank Transfer, Card & Cash Limits
seoTitle: Paying for Medical Treatment in Türkiye: Payment Guide
metaDescription: 2026 guide to paying for medical treatment in Türkiye: customs cash limits, foreign card fees, SWIFT bank transfers, and official e-Arşiv invoices.
quickAnswer: You can pay for medical treatment in Türkiye by international SWIFT bank transfer, Visa or Mastercard, or cash, though each carries distinct rules. Türkiye sets no cap on bringing foreign cash in, but departure customs rules in the EU (€10,000) and UK (£10,000) apply. Always pay the licensed provider directly and insist on an official itemized e-Arşiv invoice.

body.text: What are the customs cash declaration limits when flying into Türkiye?

Türkiye places no upper limit on the amount of foreign or Turkish currency you can bring into the country, as confirmed by the [Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Culture and Tourism](https://www.ktb.gov.tr/EN-120418/foreign-exchange.html) and [Ministry of Foreign Affairs customs guidance](https://www.mfa.gov.tr/turkiye_ye-ait-gumruk-bilgileri.en.mfa). However, your departure country still enforces strict cash declaration rules before you board.

Under [European Commission EU cash controls](https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/customs/prohibitions-restrictions/eu-cash-controls_en), travellers leaving or entering the EU with €10,000 or more in cash (or equivalent) must file a customs declaration. Travellers leaving Great Britain face a £10,000 threshold under [GOV.UK cash rules](https://www.gov.uk/bringing-cash-into-uk). If you later leave Türkiye with unused cash, outbound Turkish rules—updated in March 2025 under Communiqué No. 2008-32/34 and summarised by [Türkkan Law Firm](https://turkkanlawfirm.com/en/library/regulatory-updates/cash-declaration-threshold-try-185000/)—require declaring amounts exceeding €10,000 in foreign banknotes or TRY 185,000 in Turkish lira.
Do Turkish hospitals charge extra for foreign credit cards or Amex?

Large accredited private hospitals in Türkiye routinely accept foreign Visa and Mastercard debit or credit cards without adding a hospital surcharge, though your home bank may charge a foreign transaction fee. Smaller clinics sometimes quote cash-only discounts or pass on card-processing fees, and American Express acceptance remains limited outside major hospital groups.

Always ask in writing before arrival whether the quoted price differs between card, bank transfer, and cash, and notify your home bank so a high-value foreign medical charge is not blocked at check-in.

body.text: How do international bank transfers (SWIFT/SEPA) work before arrival?

Türkiye is not part of the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA); the [European Payments Council list of SEPA scheme countries](https://www.europeanpaymentscouncil.eu/document-library/other/epc-list-sepa-scheme-countries) covers 41 European jurisdictions and excludes Türkiye. Therefore, sending funds from abroad to a Turkish hospital requires an international SWIFT/BIC wire transfer using the hospital's 26-character TR IBAN.

Initiate SWIFT transfers at least three to five business days before admission so funds clear before surgery day, and select the OUR fee instruction if the hospital requires the exact net invoice amount. Never wire deposits to a personal account or an unverified third-party intermediary. Verify these details before sending money:

items: Match the legal entity name: Confirm the bank account holder matches the licensed hospital or clinic name on your treatment quote.
Check the currency account: Turkish hospitals hold separate EUR, GBP, USD, and TRY IBANs; sending the wrong currency triggers conversion losses.
Confirm refund and cancellation terms: Get written terms explaining what happens if your surgeon cancels or postpones treatment after in-person examination.
Keep the MT103 / wire confirmation: Carry a printed copy to the hospital billing desk.

body.text: Why must you insist on an official itemized Turkish invoice?

An official Turkish invoice—typically issued electronically as an e-Arşiv Fatura under [Turkish Revenue Administration (GİB)](https://dijital.gib.gov.tr/) rules, explained in [Workon's 2026 e-Arşiv guide](https://workon.com.tr/en/e-archive-invoice-turkey/)—is your legal proof of payment and services received. Informal cash receipts or chat quotes carry no legal weight for insurance reimbursement, tax deductions, or formal complaints.

faq.q: Can I pay a Turkish hospital in Euros or British Pounds?
faq.a: Yes. Most international patient departments accept payments in EUR, GBP, or USD via dedicated foreign-currency bank accounts, card terminals, or cash. Ask which currency avoids double conversion.

faq.q: Should I pay the full surgical fee before arriving in Türkiye?
faq.a: Most licensed hospitals require only a modest booking deposit or no upfront payment until after your in-person consultation and pre-operative tests. Avoid paying 100% upfront without clear written refund terms.

faq.q: Why did my card decline at a clinic in Istanbul?
faq.a: Banks routinely flag large overseas healthcare transactions as potential fraud, or your daily spending limit may be lower than the treatment total. Raise your limit and pre-notify your bank before flying.

faq.q: Can I split payment between two cards or card and bank transfer?
faq.a: Usually yes. Most hospital billing desks accept split payments—such as a pre-arrival SWIFT transfer plus a card payment on admission—provided you arrange it in advance.

faq.q: What is an e-Arşiv Fatura in Türkiye?
faq.a: An e-Arşiv Fatura is the official electronic invoice regulated by Türkiye's Revenue Administration (GİB) for individual customers. It includes a verifiable tax number and serves as legal proof of payment.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye collect hospital fees on my behalf?
faq.a: No. You pay your chosen licensed hospital or clinic directly. Itinerary of Türkiye charges a separate, transparent flat fee paid solely by our clients for independent travel coordination.
